jobs.description:
About CirrusMD:

CirrusMD is redefining virtual care by delivering a Physician-first Care & Guidance solution that meets patients at their moment of need. Our text-based (or web) app connects patients with licensed physicians in under a minute, allowing them to engage in care at their own pace and convenience. Available 24/7/365, CirrusMD’s integrated care spans multiple specialties—from acute and chronic care to behavioral health. Our platform serves 10 million users across all 50 states and is offered exclusively through employers and health plans. Learn more at cirrusmd.com.

JOB SUMMARY

The Client Success Executive (CSE) is responsible for developing and maintaining exceptional relationships with internal and client partners, ensuring clients achieve maximum value from the CirrusMD platform. The CSE owns retention and growth across an assigned book of business — identifying upsell opportunities, growing membership/covered lives, and meeting utilization goals. This role involves day-to-day client management, proactive engagement to understand and address client needs, and cross-functional collaboration to drive measurable success outcomes. The ideal candidate will have a background in mid- to large-scale client relationship management within healthcare services, with demonstrated success exceeding expectations while maintaining and growing their book.

ESSENTIAL ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Percent of time spent is approximate and totals 100%.

25% — Client Value, Relationships & Implementation

  • Client Value Realization: Work closely with clients to understand their business objectives and vision, and ensure the CirrusMD platform delivers measurable value aligned with those goals; share client objectives across the CirrusMD team.
  • Client Relationship Management: Serve as the primary point of contact for assigned large, strategic accounts, managing day-to-day communications and building strong relationships with client stakeholders at all levels, up to and including the executive suite.
  • Onboarding, Implementation & Adoption: Manage intake and implementation of new projects from Client Success leadership and the Sales team; act as the key partner contact to facilitate implementation and hit go-live timelines, and drive adoption through training, best practices, and ongoing support.
  • Expectation Setting: Set proper client expectations based on knowledge of the CirrusMD platform, scope of relationship, and contractual requirements.

50% — Growth, Retention & Account Strategy

  • Client Growth & Upselling: Identify opportunities for account growth — including product upsell, cross-sell of complementary solutions, and growing membership/covered lives — and partner with Marketing to increase utilization across the book of business.
  • Retention & Renewal Management: Proactively manage client renewals, minimizing churn through ongoing engagement and demonstrated, continuous value.
  • Strategic Account Planning: Develop and maintain strategic account plans for growth and retention; strategize with clients on all opportunities to ensure solutions are being effectively utilized and expanded, and conceptualize new programs that deepen partner relationships.
  • Business Reviews & ROI Reporting: Develop and deliver business review presentations that demonstrate return on investment and program outcomes, and use ongoing review of those outcomes to recommend changes that optimize the CirrusMD platform to its full potential.
  • Client Health Monitoring: Regularly track and assess client health, using data and insights to identify risk and surface opportunities for deeper engagement and growth.
  • Performance Metrics & Reporting: Monitor key success metrics such as utilization and adoption rates, client satisfaction (NPS/CSAT), membership growth, and revenue; report progress and outcomes regularly to both clients and internal stakeholders.

25% — Collaboration, Advocacy & Market Insight

  • Issue Resolution: Act as a trusted advisor and advocate for the client, ensuring issues and concerns are addressed swiftly and effectively, coordinating with internal teams as necessary.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work closely with Sales, Sales Support, Product Management, Business Development, Marketing, and Support to ensure a seamless client experience and to complete requests for proposals/information in a timely, accurate, and professional manner.
  • Client Feedback & Product Improvement: Collect and relay client and market feedback to Product and Marketing to help inform go-to-market strategy and the roadmap for future product development.
  • Client Presentations & Site Visits: Lead client presentations and facilitate site visits; routinely present product updates and roadmap to external client stakeholders; participate in Sales finalist presentations as needed.
  • Platform & Industry Expertise: Maintain a deep understanding of CirrusMD's technical and operational set-up and how it is implemented to ensure platform optimization; stay current on company initiatives and industry trends.

SKILLS AND QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree in business or equivalent experience.
  • 5 – 7+ years of healthcare industry experience in client success, account management, consulting, sales, or other applicable area; successful selling and/or account management experience in healthcare services required.
  • Proven experience driving client outcomes and revenue growth, with executive-level relationship management experience.
  • Demonstrated ability to meet and exceed goals, and to work and manage clients independently.
  • Strong relationship-building, listening, and communication skills, capable of working with a variety of client stakeholders, including executives.
  • Experience managing large, complex client accounts and coordinating across multiple departments.
  • Ability to conduct executive-level presentations, facilitate group discussions, and deliver engaging product demonstrations.
  • Technically astute, with the ability to lead IT and other product-related discussions.
  • Analytical thinking, data-driven decision making, and strong problem-solving skills to proactively address client challenges.
  • A professional, resourceful, and results-driven style; well organized, detail oriented, and able to take initiative and manage multiple projects at a time.
  • Proficiency with CRM systems and client success platforms such as Salesforce.
  • Hands-on, strong team player, and fully accountable for delivering agreed-upon performance metrics.
  • Ability to travel up to 25% — cyclical depending on client needs.
  • Protect and take care of our company and member's data every day by committing to work within our company ethics and policies.
  • Experience with self-insured employers
  • Experience working with national broker and consulting houses

COMPENSATION

  • Salary
  • Variable compensation

  • 401(k), including company match

What's in it for you:

CirrusMD is paving the way to a better healthcare future and our work truly matters! Our solution is exceptionally accessible, instantly available, and simply scalable. If you are looking to make a lasting impact where your voice matters, consider joining our team and help us deliver care without barriers. We take the health and happiness of our employees seriously and offer great benefits including:
  • Competitive compensation
  • Deeply subsidized medical, dental & vision insurance for you and your family
  • Unlimited PTO / Vacation
  • 401(K) + match
  • Paid maternity & paternity leave
  • Remote friendly
  • Growth opportunity
  • A positive, collaborative and diverse culture

jobs.title: Director, Human Resources Operations
jobs.excerpt: Job Description:The Director of Human Resources provides leadership for the day-to-day delivery of Human Resources Operations and serves as the senior operational leader for employee relations, HR service delivery, talent acquisition support, compensation administration, compliance, and full employee lifecycle support.
jobs.description:
Job Description:

The Director of Human Resources provides leadership for the day-to-day delivery of Human Resources Operations and serves as the senior operational leader for employee relations, HR service delivery, talent acquisition support, compensation administration, compliance, and full employee lifecycle support.


Reporting to the Vice President of Human Resources, the Director translates enterprise people strategy into effective operational practices and ensures Human Resources programs, policies, processes, and services are administered consistently and effectively.


The Director provides direct leadership to the Generalist team, establishing a strong Generalist model capable of supporting leaders and employees throughout the full employee lifecycle—from workforce and recruitment needs through onboarding, development, employee relations, organizational changes, and separation.


The Director also works collaboratively with Human Resources partners across the institutions. While the role does not have direct responsibility for institutional HR operations or personnel, the Director maintains awareness of institutional needs, practices, and emerging challenges to identify opportunities for shared solutions, greater consistency, and advancement of System Office HR operations and system-wide HR standards and best practices.


The Director works closely with the Associate Vice President of HR Systems & Technology, Associate Vice President of Workforce Development & Employee Engagement, and Benefits leadership to ensure operational needs are connected to technology, process improvement, employee education, workforce development, benefits and leave practices, and broader organizational capability.


Essential Responsibilities

Human Resources Operations & Service Delivery

  • Provide leadership and oversight for day-to-day Human Resources Operations and service delivery.
  • Lead, develop, and support Senior HR Generalists and HR Generalists in providing responsive, consistent, and consultative Human Resources support throughout the employee lifecycle.
  • Establish operational priorities, service expectations, escalation practices, and accountability across HR Operations.
  • Ensure HR policies, procedures, and standard operating procedures are effectively implemented and consistently applied.
  • Identify opportunities to streamline practices, improve service delivery, strengthen controls, and reduce unnecessary administrative processes.
  • Monitor operational metrics, trends, service needs, and recurring challenges to identify opportunities for continuous improvement.
  • Maintain appropriate documentation, controls, and audit readiness across HR operational processes.
  • Partner with HR Systems & Technology to identify opportunities for workflow improvement, automation, and enhanced employee and manager self-service.

Generalist Leadership

  • Provide direct leadership, coaching, development, and performance management to Senior HR Generalists and HR Generalists.
  • Establish clear roles, responsibilities, decision-making authority, and escalation protocols within the Generalist function.
  • Develop a comprehensive Generalist model that provides support across the full employee lifecycle.
  • Strengthen Generalist capability in employee relations, manager consultation, recruiting and onboarding, investigations, performance management, compliance, organizational change, and HR judgment.
  • Assign and prioritize work based on organizational needs, complexity, risk, institutional support needs, and team capacity.
  • Create opportunities for Generalists to develop deeper areas of expertise while maintaining broad HR capabilities.
  • Promote consistency in how HR practices, policies, processes, and employee matters are addressed.
  • Ensure Generalists have the education, tools, systems knowledge, and resources necessary to effectively support employees and leaders.

Full Employee Lifecycle Support

  • Ensure effective HR operational support throughout the employee lifecycle, including workforce needs, recruitment, hiring, onboarding, employment changes, performance management, development, employee relations, and separation.
  • Establish consistent processes and service expectations for key employee lifecycle activities.
  • Ensure Generalists provide effective consultation and coordination to hiring managers throughout recruitment and selection processes.
  • Support recruitment strategy, candidate experience, selection practices, offer development, and hiring processes.
  • Ensure onboarding practices effectively connect new employees to their positions, managers, organizational expectations, systems, resources, and culture.
  • Monitor employee lifecycle processes to identify gaps, inefficiencies, or opportunities for improved employee and manager experience.
  • Partner with HR Systems & Technology and Workforce Development & Employee Engagement to continuously improve the employee experience across the lifecycle.

Employee Relations & Employment Risk

  • Provide leadership for employee relations matters, including performance management, corrective action, workplace concerns, investigations, conflict resolution, and separations.
  • Serve as the primary operational escalation point for complex employee relations matters within System Office HR Operations.
  • Ensure investigations and employee relations matters are handled objectively, consistently, timely, and in accordance with organizational policy and applicable employment requirements.
  • Assess employment-related risk and determine when matters warrant consultation with the Vice President of Human Resources, Legal Counsel, or other leadership.
  • Consult with managers and HR partners regarding performance expectations, documentation, corrective action, and employee relations strategy.
  • Analyze employee relations activity for recurring trends that may indicate broader policy, process, leadership development, education, or workforce needs.

Institutional HR Partnership & System Alignment

  • Build collaborative relationships with Human Resources leaders and partners across the institutions to strengthen communication, coordination, and shared understanding across the HR community.
  • Maintain awareness of institutional HR priorities, operational needs, challenges, and emerging practices without assuming direct management responsibility for institutional HR teams or institution-specific decisions.
  • Create opportunities for institutional HR partners to provide input into enterprise HR processes, policies, systems, and initiatives.
  • Identify common needs, recurring challenges, and successful practices that can inform system-wide HR solutions.
  • Promote greater consistency in HR practices where standardization creates organizational value while recognizing legitimate institutional differences and operational requirements.
  • Advance shared HR standards, tools, resources, and best practices across System Office and the institutions.
  • Facilitate knowledge sharing and collaboration across the HR community to reduce duplication and leverage expertise throughout the system.
  • Partner with the Vice President of Human Resources to identify opportunities to strengthen overall HR capability and systemness.

Organizational Change & Workforce Planning

  • Provide operational HR leadership and consultation for reorganizations, restructures, position changes, workforce transitions, and other organizational initiatives within the Director's scope.
  • Ensure appropriate consideration of business rationale, employee impact, job responsibilities, compensation, employment risk, implementation readiness, and communication needs.
  • Partner with institutional HR leadership on enterprise processes and standards associated with organizational changes while respecting institutional decision-making responsibilities.
  • Coordinate with the Vice President of Human Resources, Legal Affairs, Finance, and other partners on matters requiring additional review.
  • Identify workforce trends and operational needs that should inform broader workforce planning and organizational strategy.

Compensation

  • Lead operational administration of compensation programs in alignment with established compensation philosophy and enterprise strategy.
  • Oversee job evaluation, market pricing, salary recommendations, promotional increases, position changes, and compensation analysis.
  • Promote internal consistency, market awareness, and equitable application of compensation practices.
  • Provide compensation consultation and resources to institutional HR partners and organizational leaders.
  • Partner with the Vice President of Human Resources on compensation strategy, significant exceptions, annual compensation planning, and matters requiring executive review.
  • Support development and maintenance of salary structures, compensation guidelines, processes, tools, and education.

Benefits & Leave Partnership

  • Maintain a strong collaborative partnership with Benefits leadership to support an integrated employee experience across HR Operations, benefits, retirement, and leave administration.
  • Ensure Generalists and Institutional Partners understand appropriate benefits and leave processes, resources, and escalation pathways so employees and managers are connected to the appropriate support.
  • Partner on employee matters where benefits, leave, accommodations, employee relations, or other HR operational considerations intersect.
  • Coordinate with Benefits leadership to identify recurring employee or manager questions that may indicate a need for additional communication, education, or process improvement.
  • Support consistent communication and coordination among HR Operations, Benefits, Payroll, HR Systems, institutional HR teams, and external partners.
  • Provide operational feedback to Benefits leadership and the Vice President of Human Resources regarding employee and manager experiences with benefits and leave processes.

The Director does not have direct oversight or accountability for Benefits; these functions remain separately led within the Human Resources structure.

Workforce Development & Employee Engagement Partnership

  • Partner closely with the Associate Vice President of Workforce Development & Employee Engagement to connect operational trends and organizational needs with workforce development priorities.
  • Translate insights from employee relations, Generalists, recruitment, performance management, and institutional HR partners into potential learning, leadership, engagement, and organizational development needs.
  • Support implementation and adoption of performance management, leadership development, employee engagement, internal mobility, career development, talent management, and related enterprise initiatives.
  • Establish feedback loops between HR Operations and Workforce Development to evaluate effectiveness, identify barriers, and continuously improve programs.
  • Ensure Generalists understand enterprise workforce development initiatives and can reinforce available resources and programs through their interactions with employees and managers.
  • Help ensure workforce development initiatives are practical, relevant, and responsive to needs being observed across the organization.

HR Systems, Process Improvement & Education

  • Partner with the Associate Vice President of HR Systems & Technology to ensure HR systems and processes effectively support operational and institutional needs.
  • Identify system enhancements, automation opportunities, reporting needs, and process improvements based on operational experience and feedback.
  • Strengthen education and communication regarding HR systems, policies, procedures, and standardized processes.
  • Ensure Generalists understand available technology, established workflows, and enterprise standards so they can effectively support managers and employees.
  • Partner with institutional HR teams to identify where additional system or process education may improve adoption and consistency.
  • Use HR data and people analytics to identify trends, evaluate effectiveness, and inform operational recommendations.
  • Support ongoing maintenance and continuous improvement of HR processes and initiatives following initial implementation.

Leadership & Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Promote collaboration across HR Operations, HR Systems & Technology, Workforce Development & Employee Engagement, Benefits, institutional HR teams, and organizational partners.
  • Create an environment in which operational information is routinely shared and translated into opportunities for improvement.
  • Support development of an increasingly connected HR community that shares knowledge, tools, expertise, education, and best practices.
  • Balance enterprise consistency with institutional needs when evaluating HR practices and recommendations.
  • Foster a culture of accountability, service, continuous improvement, collaboration, and shared responsibility across Human Resources.

Decision-Making & Escalation Authority

The Director of Human Resources is expected to independently lead and resolve routine and complex HR operational matters within established policies, practices, and organizational guidelines.

The Director serves as the primary operational escalation point for the Senior HR Generalists and HR Generalist. Matters should generally be escalated to the Vice President of Human Resources when they involve:

  • Significant enterprise, legal, financial, or reputational risk
  • Executive-level employees or leadership matters
  • Significant organizational restructures or workforce actions
  • Decisions establishing substantial organizational precedent
  • Major exceptions to established compensation or HR practices
  • Enterprise policy or governance decisions
  • Significant institutional or cross-system implications
  • Matters requiring Executive Leadership or Board consideration

The Director's collaborative relationship with institutional HR partners does not replace institutional reporting relationships or decision-making authority. The Director serves as a resource, connector, and operational partner to strengthen shared HR practices, identify enterprise opportunities, advance consistency where appropriate, and strengthen system-wide HR capability.

Direct Reports

  • Senior HR Generalist (2)
  • HR Generalist

Key Partnerships

  • Vice President, Human Resources
  • Associate Vice President, HR Systems & Technology
  • Associate Vice President, Workforce Development & Employee Engagement
  • Benefits Leadership
  • Institutional Human Resources Leadership and HR Partners
  • Legal Affairs
  • Finance and Payroll
  • Information Technology
  • Institutional and System Office Leadership

Knowledge & Skills

  • Advanced knowledge of Human Resources operations, employee relations, employment practices, and HR compliance.
  • Strong understanding of the full employee lifecycle and consultative HR practices.
  • Demonstrated ability to assess complex employee and organizational matters and exercise sound judgment.
  • Knowledge of compensation, talent acquisition, performance management, workforce planning, benefits, and leave practices.
  • Strong understanding of organizational change and workforce transition processes.
  • Ability to recognize operational patterns and translate them into recommendations for process, systems, education, or workforce development improvements.
  • Demonstrated ability to collaborate and influence across decentralized or matrixed organizations without relying on direct authority.
  • Strong communication, consultation, conflict resolution, and relationship-building skills.
  • Ability to balance enterprise standards and consistency with legitimate institutional needs and differences.
  • Strong project management, prioritization, and continuous improvement capabilities.
  • Experience with Workday and other HR technology for data-informed decision-making.

Education

  • Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Organizational Leadership, or a related field required.
  • Master's degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Organizational Development, or a related field preferred.

Experience

  • Minimum of 8–10 years of progressively responsible Human Resources experience.
  • Minimum of 3–5 years of HR leadership or management experience.
  • Significant experience in employee relations, HR operations, and consultative Human Resources support required.
  • Experience supporting the full employee lifecycle, including talent acquisition, onboarding, employee relations, performance management, and separation.
  • Experience supporting organizational restructuring, workforce planning, and complex employment matters strongly preferred.
  • Experience working within a multi-location, multi-state, higher education, system-based, or similarly complex organization preferred.
  • Demonstrated experience leading and developing HR professionals and collaborating with HR colleagues across decentralized or matrixed environments.

Working Conditions

  • While not required, residence within a reasonable commuting distance of a Community office or campus is preferred to support opportunities for in-person collaboration and engagement.
  • Ability to travel up to 20%, including travel to Community offices, campuses, meetings, and other business-related events as needed.
  • Ability to effectively perform the responsibilities of the position in a remote work environment and maintain availability during established business hours, with flexibility as required to support organizational needs across locations and time zones.

Compensation & Benefits

This opportunity is budgeted at $120,000 - 125,000 base compensation. Additional compensation factors may impact total compensation. To learn more about our competitive benefits and additional rewards, including generous paid time-off, medical and dental insurance coverage, life and disability insurance, retirement plan with employer contribution, multiple flexible spending accounts, tuition reimbursement, click the link below.

The Community Solution is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

Application Process

Please note the screening, recruitment, and selection process is managed by recruiting staff and hiring managers with the aid of artificial intelligence to evaluate candidates against job requirements. The artificial intelligence tool is a resource only and all employment decisions are made by staff members.

When you apply, it is recommended you utilize the option to parse your resume into the application. To ensure your experience is accurately reflected, please review and complete all application fields—even if you auto-fill from your resume.

For the best results, tailor your resume to the job description, highlight key qualifications and skills, and use clear, consistent formatting. This helps our AI tools read and assess your application more effectively. We are committed to regularly monitoring the process for fairness and remove personally identifiable information during evaluation.

jobs.description:
Arise is a globally active weight-loss app with over 10 million downloads and a 4.6 rating on the App Store. Our mission is simple but ambitious: empower millions of people to become healthier and happier.

We're looking for a CTO who is a true architect on both iOS and Android — someone deeply skilled in iOS who can take full ownership of our existing app and raise it further, and who can also build our Android app from scratch. You'll develop primarily through AI rather than by hand, and you'll thrive on ownership, precision, and long-term thinking. This role is for someone who ships high-quality code today while foreseeing how today's decisions shape the app for years ahead — technically, strategically, and financially.

Today Arise is iOS-only, so this is where you'll start and where you'll prove yourself: owning, deepening, and future-proofing a mature codebase used by millions. From there, you'll architect and build our Android app from the ground up.

If you excel at structured, autonomous work, build with AI as your default way of working, understand the importance of monetization, and want to own the technology behind a product used by millions, we'd love to hear from you.

Your Role

  • Own and architect the existing iOS app — maintain, optimize, deepen, and future-proof a codebase used by millions.
  • Build the Arise Android app from scratch — architecture, delivery, and long-term ownership.
  • Ensure cross-platform consistency and a coherent technical vision across both platforms.
  • Develop and test features that enhance the Arise experience.
  • Use AI agents and automated workflows as your primary means of building, testing, and shipping — not as an occasional helper.
  • Anticipate technical pitfalls and proactively design solutions.
  • Collaborate with design to refine usability for a smooth user experience.
  • Support monetization by integrating features with measurable business impact.

Requirements

  • Proven track record architecting and shipping production mobile apps, ideally as a senior engineer, lead, or technical founder.
  • Deep, architect-level iOS expertise — you can own a mature codebase end to end and make the hard structural calls with confidence.
  • Demonstrated ability to build an Android app from scratch to the same standard.
  • Hands-on fluency building through AI — agentic coding tools, LLM-driven workflows, automated testing and release. You've actually shipped this way, not just experimented.
  • Excellent problem-solving and critical-thinking skills.
  • Comfortable working fully in English.

Technical Skills

  • Expert-level iOS/Swift — architecture, patterns, performance, and the judgment to keep a large app maintainable as it grows.
  • Strong Android development (Kotlin) with the ability to architect a new app end to end.
  • Familiarity with mobile build and release tooling (e.g. Fastlane).
  • Deep understanding of Apple and Android design principles, patterns, and best practices.
  • Ability to write clean, well-documented, maintainable code — and to direct AI to do the same.

Who You Are

  • A decisive builder who takes a problem and runs with it — you'd rather ship and iterate than wait for certainty.
  • Direct and results-driven, comfortable owning outcomes and making the call.
  • Energized by autonomy and full ownership of the technology.
  • Allergic to bureaucracy — "meetings that should have been emails" are your enemy.

Why You'll Love Working with Us

  • High autonomy: own the entire tech stack from idea to release.
  • Clear decision-making with minimal bureaucracy.
  • Work with the newest hardware and technologies.
  • Complimentary Claude Max subscription.
  • Flexible, remote-first role (full-time).
  • Paid annual leave.
  • Direct collaboration with the founder — your work will have visible impact from day one.

How to Apply

Send us your application including:

  • Your CV
  • A history of the mobile apps you've built (iOS and Android)
  • Salary expectations
  • (Optional) Code samples or GitHub repositories

Help us build and refine a product that runs like a well-oiled machine — and improves millions of lives in the process.

Patient Care Coordinator

Job Summary

The Patient Care Coordinator supports the organization’s population health and value-based care initiatives by proactively identifying and closing gaps in patient care. This position is responsible for coordinating patient outreach, scheduling Medicare Annual Wellness Visits and other preventive services, supporting chronic care management initiatives, and coordinating wellness and population health projects.

The Patient Care Coordinator works closely with patients, providers, clinical staff, and administrative teams to improve patient access, preventive care, quality outcomes, and overall patient engagement. The position requires excellent communication, organization, attention to detail, follow-through, and the ability to work independently while maintaining strong collaborative relationships across the organization.

Duties and Responsibilities

Patient Outreach & Gap Closure

  • Identify patients with open preventive, chronic care, and quality-of-care gaps through designated reports, registries, and electronic health record systems.

  • Conduct proactive patient outreach by telephone and other approved communication methods to address identified care gaps.

  • Educate patients regarding recommended preventive services, screenings, immunizations, and routine healthcare needs.

  • Schedule patients for appropriate services and follow up as needed to ensure completion.

  • Document all patient outreach, scheduling, and care-gap activities accurately and timely in the appropriate systems.

  • Collaborate with providers, nurses, medical assistants, and other staff to resolve barriers to care.

  • Monitor assigned patient populations and follow up on outstanding gaps to support organizational quality goals and value-based care initiatives.

  • Assist with tracking and reporting care-gap closure progress.

Wellness Visit Coordination

  • Coordinate and schedule Medicare Annual Wellness Visits and other preventive wellness appointments.

  • Conduct patient outreach to educate eligible patients about the importance and benefits of wellness visits.

  • Maintain and utilize scheduling lists, reports, and tracking tools to identify patients due or overdue for wellness services.

  • Coordinate with clinic staff and providers to ensure appropriate scheduling and preparation for wellness visits.

  • Follow up with patients who are unable to schedule or complete their wellness visit.

  • Assist in developing and maintaining processes designed to improve wellness visit completion rates.

Wellness & Population Health Projects

  • Coordinate assigned wellness and population health projects from planning through completion.

  • Assist with developing patient outreach lists, tracking spreadsheets, reports, educational materials, and other project resources.

  • Coordinate communication between departments and team members involved in wellness initiatives.

  • Monitor project progress and communicate barriers, needs, and outcomes to leadership.

  • Participate in quality improvement initiatives designed to improve patient outcomes and organizational performance.

  • Assist with special projects related to preventive care, quality measures, patient engagement, and value-based care.

Chronic Care Management Support

  • Coordinate assigned chronic care management projects and patient outreach initiatives.

  • Assist in identifying eligible patients and supporting enrollment or engagement activities as directed.

  • Conduct outreach to patients regarding chronic disease management needs, follow-up appointments, preventive services, and recommended care.

  • Coordinate with clinical staff to ensure identified patient needs are communicated appropriately.

  • Track assigned chronic care management activities and maintain accurate documentation.

  • Assist with identifying opportunities to improve patient engagement, continuity of care, and chronic disease outcomes.

Professional Requirements & Expectations

The Patient Care Coordinator is expected to consistently demonstrate professionalism, reliability, accountability, and a commitment to patient-centered care.

  • Ensures that appearance and personal conduct are professional at all times.

  • Maintains an excellent attendance record and demonstrates reliability and punctuality.

  • Wears appropriate clothing for assigned job functions and wears the required organization ID badge.

  • Works to maintain a positive rapport and cooperative working relationship with physicians, administration, clinical staff, and coworkers.

  • Demonstrates respect, courtesy, and professionalism in all interactions.

  • Represents the organization positively and professionally in the community.

  • Maintains patient confidentiality at all times and protects patient information in accordance with HIPAA and organizational policies.

  • Complies with all organizational policies regarding ethical business practices.

  • Maintains HIPAA compliance in all patient interactions, documentation, communication, and use of electronic systems.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Previous experience in a healthcare, medical office, care coordination, population health, or patient outreach setting.

  • Experience with electronic health records and healthcare scheduling systems.

  • Experience with patient outreach, quality measures, care-gap closure, wellness visits, or chronic care management preferred.

  • Knowledge of Medicare preventive services and value-based care concepts preferred.

  • Strong computer, organizational, communication, and customer service skills.

  • Ability to manage multiple projects and priorities while meeting established deadlines.

jobs.description:
About the role

Location: Anywhere in Canada, remote (with an option to work from an office in Victoria, Vancouver, Edmonton or Toronto)

Hours: 37.5 hours per week (Flexible, open to a shorter week with pro-rated salary)

Starting salary:$123,600-$133,900 FTE

Type: Full-time, permanent

Start date: Negotiable, ideally January 2027

Application deadline: 11:59 p.m. PT, Friday, October 2, 2026

Over the past eight years, The Narwhal has pioneered non-profit journalism in Canada, growing our revenue ten-fold, building a thriving membership program of 7,500 recurring donors and earning the support of more than a dozen philanthropic foundations. Now with an annual budget of more than $4 million, we are hiring our first Director of Philanthropy, who will help to build the relationships needed to sustain and grow our independent journalism.

Working closely with The Narwhal’s co-founder and executive director, the Director of Philanthropy will lead The Narwhal’s revenue strategy and fundraising operations with a focus on growing foundation giving and major gifts. (The Narwhal’s audience department is primarily responsible for its thriving membership program.)

The Director of Philanthropy will oversee development strategy and execution, including institutional philanthropy, major gifts, donor communications, events strategy, grants management and revenue forecasting. Prior journalism experience is not required — we are excited to hear from candidates in adjacent fields with applicable strategic and fundraising experience with a passion for independent media.

Responsibilities

Strategic Planning and Leadership

  • Work collaboratively with the Executive Director, Director of Operations and Finance and Director of Audience, to develop an annual fund development plan and calendar to coordinate all fundraising activities to maximize results
  • Partner with the Executive Director and leadership team to create and implement new initiatives to achieve the organization’s impact goals and attract financial support
  • Lead cross-departmental collaboration to align organizational priorities and fundraising opportunities
  • Track and analyze fundraising metrics to test and learn, implementing lessons
  • Manage, mentor and support the Development Coordinator, setting clear priorities and supporting their professional growth
  • Ensure fundraising practices uphold The Narwhal’s values, donor privacy and editorial independence

Revenue Strategy

  • Evaluate The Narwhal’s current fundraising capabilities, identify strengths and gaps and build a map of future revenue potential
  • Working with the Director of Operations and Finance, develop fundraising revenue forecasts and budgets, monitor performance and provide regular reporting to the Executive Director and leadership team
  • Develop a diversified fundraising portfolio that is resilient, recession- and loss-resistant and sustainable, spanning legacy gifts, donor-advised funds, foundation giving and major gifts

Foundation grants

  • Build and maintain relationships with a wide range of foundations, aligning funding priorities with The Narwhal’s goals
  • Establish and develop relationships with new foundations to grow the organization’s grant revenue
  • Lead all stages of grant development and management, from prospect research and project scoping to grant writing, budgeting and reporting
  • Develop and maintain an institutional giving pipeline and calendar, with rigorous follow-up and stewardship
  • Establish internal grant-writing processes, templates and workflows to strengthen efficiency and consistency

Major Donor Cultivation

  • Develop goals and strategies for cultivation, solicitation and stewardship for major donors, with a goal to increase revenue
  • Oversee prospect research and identify opportunities to bring new supporters into the organization and increase giving from existing donors
  • Support the Executive Director’s donor engagement and carry out direct engagement with donors and prospects as necessary
  • Oversee the planning and management of strategic cultivation and stewardship events

Required skills & experience

  • You have a minimum of 10 years’ senior-level experience working directly for a foundation or successfully fundraising from foundations and major donors for an organization with annual revenue of at least $3 million
  • You’ve raised money from both individuals and foundations and you can point to donor and funder relationships you built rather than inherited
  • You have a track record of personally cultivating, soliciting and closing major gifts and multi-year foundation commitments, with a portfolio in the range of $2 million+/year
  • You write well, whether it’s a proposal, email or a briefing note for tomorrow’s meeting
  • You have experience managing, mentoring and supporting fundraising staff and/or cross-functional teams
  • You have built and led effective teams during periods of organizational growth and evolution
  • You are comfortable representing an organization in high-level external settings and capable of building trust with a broad array of stakeholders
  • You can see the long-term strategic picture while also building the systems required to deliver results
  • You have a proven track record in writing successful grant proposals and grant reporting
  • You are experienced with fundraising databases and project management tools. (Bonus points for Salesforce and Airtable experience!)

You’ll stand out if

  • You can explain why journalism matters to someone who’s never thought about it, even if you’ve never worked in journalism
  • You are well-connected to foundations and donors who care about the environment
  • You have your CFRE certification

Working Conditions

  • Regular computer-based work, including donor and prospect research, reporting and written correspondence
  • Regular communication with donors, foundations, staff and other external partners by email, phone video conference and in-person meetings
  • Occasional evening or weekend work may be required for fundraising, donor stewardship and events
  • Regular travel within Canada is required for donor and foundation meetings, organizational meetings and special events

We offer the following benefits

  • Group health, vision and dental benefits and a health spending account
  • A flexible workplace with a vibrant, collaborative culture
  • Work-from-home stipend or work from a shared office in Victoria, Vancouver, Edmonton or Toronto
  • GRSP base contributions after three months
  • Four weeks of vacation per year, plus your birthday off
  • 10 personal days per year
  • Organization-wide holiday shutdown
  • Professional development opportunities and fund
  • Two-month top-up program for EI-protected leaves

When it comes to compensation, research shows wide disparities in how candidates negotiate, which is partially responsible for wage gaps between groups of people. At The Narwhal we have a transparent and competitive salary grid for our entire team. We developed this approach because we wanted to remove the guesswork around compensation and put everyone on an equal footing. The posted salary range is in line with our grid and is not negotiable.

How to apply

To apply, please submit a cover letter and résumé by 11:59 p.m. Friday, October 2, 2026, at the latest. Please include your full name in the file name of any attachments you submit. In your cover letter please tell us why specifically you want to work at The Narwhal and what from your previous experience makes you a good fit for this role.

Applicants must be eligible to work in Canada. We thank all applicants for their interest; however, only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

The Narwhal is working to build an inclusive and equitable team that reflects the communities we serve. People who identify as being from marginalized communities, including Indigenous Peoples, racialized people, people with disabilities, people identifying as 2SLGBTQ+, and people from low-income backgrounds are especially encouraged to apply. Disability-related accommodations are available for candidates taking part in our hiring process. We will ask candidates selected for an interview about any accessibility needs ahead of the scheduled interview.

What to expect

We want candidates to have a clear sense of what’s ahead and when they can expect to hear from us. Here’s our anticipated hiring timeline:

  • Week of October 4: Candidates will be invited to an initial video meeting with our People operations specialist to learn a little more about each other and the role
  • Week of October 18: First-round interviews will take place
  • Week of October 25: Selected candidates will complete a paid assignment
  • Week of November 1: Selected candidates will move forward to second-round interviews
  • Following the second round: We may invite finalists to an additional conversation before making our decision — if a third interview is needed, we’ll let candidates know as early as possible

All interviews will take place virtually. We’ll keep candidates updated throughout the process so you know where things stand and what to expect.

Salary: $123,600-$133,900 FTE

jobs.description:
Position Overview

The Chief Learning Officer (CLO) is responsible for leading the organization's enterprise-wide learning, development, and workforce capability strategy. The CLO drives a culture of continuous learning by designing and implementing programs that enhance employee skills, leadership capabilities, performance, and organizational effectiveness. This role ensures the workforce remains future-ready by aligning learning initiatives with business objectives, digital transformation efforts, and evolving industry demands.

Key Responsibilities

Learning & Development Strategy

Develop and execute a comprehensive enterprise learning and development strategy aligned with business goals.

Establish a culture of continuous learning, innovation, and professional growth.

Identify future workforce capabilities and skills required to support organizational success.

Leadership Development & Succession Planning

Design and implement leadership development programs for emerging, mid-level, and senior leaders.

Support succession planning initiatives to strengthen leadership pipelines.

Develop executive coaching and mentoring programs.

Talent Development & Workforce Capability

Assess organizational skills gaps and implement targeted development initiatives.

Create learning pathways that support career progression and internal mobility.

Drive workforce upskilling and reskilling initiatives.

Learning Technologies & Digital Learning

Oversee learning management systems (LMS), digital learning platforms, and educational technologies.

Leverage e-learning, microlearning, AI-driven learning tools, and virtual training solutions.

Ensure accessibility and scalability of learning programs across the organization.

Organizational Effectiveness

Partner with business leaders to align learning initiatives with strategic priorities.

Support organizational transformation and change management through learning interventions.

Improve employee productivity and performance through targeted development programs.

Performance & Learning Analytics

Develop metrics and KPIs to measure learning effectiveness and business impact.

Monitor employee participation, skill development, certification attainment, and performance outcomes.

Use analytics to continuously improve learning programs.

Compliance & Regulatory Training

Ensure delivery of mandatory compliance, regulatory, and risk management training.

Maintain records and reporting to support audit and compliance requirements.

Partner with legal, compliance, and risk teams to ensure training effectiveness.

Stakeholder Collaboration

Collaborate with HR, talent management, operations, technology, and business leaders.

Engage external training providers, universities, professional bodies, and industry partners.

Support employer branding through workforce development initiatives.

Innovation & Knowledge Management

Promote knowledge-sharing practices across the organization.

Develop learning communities, mentorship programs, and centers of excellence.

Introduce innovative approaches to employee learning and development.

Leadership & Team Development

Lead and mentor learning and development teams.

Build high-performing learning organizations capable of supporting enterprise growth.

Foster a culture of excellence, accountability, and continuous improvement.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Education, Organizational Development, Business Administration, Psychology, or related field; Master's degree preferred.

12–15+ years of progressive experience in learning and development, talent management, organizational development, or workforce transformation roles.

Proven experience leading enterprise learning strategies and leadership development programs.

Strong understanding of adult learning principles, instructional design, and learning technologies.

Key Skills & Competencies

Strategic learning and workforce development expertise.

Leadership development and succession planning capabilities.

Strong organizational development and change management skills.

Expertise in learning technologies and digital learning platforms.

Excellent communication, coaching, and facilitation skills.

Analytical and data-driven decision-making abilities.

Executive stakeholder management and influence.

Performance Metrics

Employee learning participation and completion rates.

Leadership pipeline strength and succession readiness.

Workforce upskilling and reskilling outcomes.

Learning program effectiveness and ROI.

Employee engagement and development satisfaction scores.

Compliance training completion and audit results.

Organizational capability and productivity improvements.

Ideal Background

Candidates typically come from:

Corporate Learning & Development Leadership

Talent Development & Organizational Development

Human Resources Executive Leadership

Leadership Development & Executive Coaching

Higher Education & Corporate Training

Learning Technology & Workforce Transformation

Consulting Firms specializing in Talent and Organizational Effectiveness

jobs.excerpt: About BJAKThe original mission of BJAK is we believe people deserve smarter ways to plan, save and grow their money.
jobs.description:
About BJAK

The original mission of BJAK is we believe people deserve smarter ways to plan, save and grow their money. This is the origin of our name.

Started in 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, its the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

Today, we are expanding ways to help people in the region — this includes spending, saving, investing, exchanging, travelling, and more. Our mission is help people get more from their money every day.

We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities from our offices and remotely, who truly enjoys their work. We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few.

If you're this person, we'd love to talk to you.

The Role

We are looking for a Business Unit Head to build and lead a business from end to end.

You will own the P&L, product, team and execution. You will identify opportunities, decide what to build, hire the team, launch and improve products, and drive growth and profitability.

This is a hands-on operating role with direct accountability for business results.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Own P&L, business strategy, targets and overall performance

  • Identify customer needs and commercial opportunities, and decide what products and features to build

  • Work directly with product, engineering and design teams to build and launch products

  • Build the team - hire strong people, set clear goals and manage performance

  • Drive user growth, engagement, revenue and profitability

  • Build partnerships and operations required to launch and scale the business

  • Make decisions quickly, solve problems directly and own execution from idea to results

What We're Looking For

  • Strong track record building, launching or scaling a product, business or business unit

  • Experience owning P&L, revenue, growth or other measurable business outcomes

  • Strong product and commercial judgement

  • Ability to work across product, engineering, operations and commercial functions

  • Experience building and leading strong teams

  • Hands-on approach - comfortable moving between strategy and detailed execution

  • Strong ownership, speed and ability to operate with limited structure

  • Experience in fintech, consumer technology or AI is an advantage

jobs.description:
About ev.energy
We are building the world's largest EV-centric virtual power plant (VPP). By connecting to vehicles, chargers, batteries, solar, and other distributed energy resources, we turn households into flexible grid assets that balance supply and demand, preventing blackouts and reducing reliance on fossil fuels.
We are scaling rapidly across North America and Europe. We are moving fast, we are AI-first, and we are looking for builders who want to power the grid of the future.

About the role
ev.energy grows through partnerships: with utilities, with the commercial team selling into them, and with the hardware and integration partners whose devices connect to our platform. We're hiring a Technical Program Manager to own those relationships end-to-end — the connective tissue between our commercial team, our external partners, and our engineering and product teams.

What you’ll do

  • Own a portfolio of technical partner relationships (roughly 6–10 to start), inheriting integration-partner relationship management as it moves into the team — the trusted bridge between what partners and commercial need and what engineering delivers
  • Lead complex integrations from requirements discovery and scoping through project planning, testing, and launch to production
  • Champion the value of our platform APIs and integrations — conveying use cases, benefits, and the integration process to partners and internal stakeholders alike
  • Coordinate across Product, Engineering, Commercial, and Support to keep everyone aligned on the critical path and on schedule
  • Develop repeatable playbooks so each new integration is faster and more reliable than the last
  • Define partner-success metrics beyond uptime and SLAs, and communicate program status, risks, and ROI to leadership
AI-first ways of working
  • Use AI tooling (Claude and equivalents) as a core part of how you work — drafting partner-facing docs and integration specs, synthesizing status across programs, and turning your playbooks into repeatable, partly-automated workflows
  • We're an AI-first company with agentic routines and shared internal tooling; you'll lean on it to stay on top of a broad portfolio and help shape how program management works in an AI-native org

What we're looking for

  • 5+ years in technical program management, product management, partnerships, or a related role
  • Strong technical fluency — comfortable with REST APIs, authentication, and integration patterns (e.g. OpenADR, DERMS, utility platforms) — paired with a genuine commercial mindset
  • Excellent external communication: you can lead a technical overview for a partner and a status update for an exec with equal ease
  • A demonstrated ability to align cross-functional stakeholders and drive commitments without direct authority
Also nice to have
  • Experience in energy, EV, IoT, or another partner-integration-heavy domain
  • A track record of building the program-management function at a small or scaling company, not just running project

Salary, benefits & how we work

The salary range for this role is $108,000-$132,300 USD.

Key benefits include:
  • Cash amount of up to 10% of your monthly salary, to cover the cost of buying or leasing an EV
  • Equity - you'll own a part of the business through our share options program
  • Healthcare options - to help keep you and your family in tip-top condition (provided by Cigna & Guardian)
  • Life and disability insurance
  • Co-working access via WeWork (if you'd like it)
  • Annual 'Team Week' whole company offsite
  • L&D allowance of $1,300 per year - everyone is learning, developing and challenging themselves so we have a professional development fund per year for you to learn new skills
You can find out more about our full range of perks and benefits here.

Location & how we work
This role is fully remote in the US, but we're specifically looking for someone based in EST.
The majority of people at ev.energy work on a fully remote basis, with a small number of roles based on-site in our testing sites.
This means that most of our people work from home, but we're happy to provide co-working subscriptions if you'd like to spend time at a WeWork (or other co-working space close to you).
We balance our remote set up by getting everyone together once a year for an offsite, as we know that spending time together IRL is super important.

Belonging at ev.energy
We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity: we do not discriminate based on race, religion, colour, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status or disability status. jobs.description:
At Gardens Interactive, we're building games centered on connection, collective adventure, and emergent stories. We believe the spirit with which we build games is reflected in the experiences our players have. The way we collaborate, solve problems, navigate uncertainty, and care for one another ultimately shapes the worlds we create. We're creating magical, shared experiences that bring players together and we know those experiences come from teams that are curious, resilient, ambitious, and deeply committed to one another.

We're a fully remote studio that embraces collaboration, thoughtful iteration, and the courage to explore new ideas. If you're excited by solving difficult problems with kind, talented teammates, and want to help build worlds where friendships flourish, we'd love to meet you.

As a Technical Level Designer, you will create worlds and sandboxes filled with opportunities to play. You are a level designer by craft, with the technical skills to build gameplay features in Unreal Engine using Blueprints and/or C++.

You will create new world affordances: gameplay verbs, activities, challenges, and interactions that invite players to experiment and engage with their surroundings. You will prototype, validate, iterate on, and deliver these features, then use them to build levels that encourage exploration, problem-solving, and memorable multiplayer moments.

A Day In The Life:

  • Rapidly prototype and validate new gameplay verbs, activities, and environmental interactions in Unreal Engine for online multiplayer.

  • Build and refine levels using the mechanics and tools you create alongside existing systems, hazards, and enemies.

  • Playtest with the team to understand how players discover and use these affordances, then refine levels and features to encourage experimentation and memorable moments.

What You’ll Do:

  • Own the design, implementation, debugging, polish, and maintenance of interactive world features and environmental gameplay toys that offer new choices, challenges, and benefits. Creature and NPC behaviors are outside this role.

  • Build levels from blockout through delivery, shaping flow, pacing, navigation, and readability across exploration, puzzles, traversal, and encounters.

  • Create reusable, configurable gameplay components and tools that help designers build and iterate on levels efficiently.

  • Rapidly prototype and playtest ideas to validate their potential, refine features, and manage scope and complexity.

  • Collaborate across disciplines to align with design direction, integrate player abilities and creature encounters, and meet technical requirements.

  • Partner with Engineering to resolve performance issues and ensure reliable multiplayer behavior.

  • Keep implementations organized and document features and tools so the team can use, tune, and maintain them.

What You’ll Bring:

  • Strong level design fundamentals in spatial composition, flow, pacing, and player guidance for open-world exploration and multiplayer play.

  • At least one shipped game as a level designer on a multidisciplinary team.

  • Proficiency in Unreal Engine Blueprints and/or C++, with the ability to independently prototype, implement, and debug gameplay features.

  • Experience building levels and authoring collision and navigation in Unreal Engine.

  • Strong playtesting and iteration habits, with an understanding of how design shapes player behavior, cooperation, and relationships.

  • Clear communication, strong collaboration, and the judgment to work independently, recognize constraints, and seek support when needed.

Nice to Have:

  • Experience building reusable level design tools, modular gameplay kits, or procedural workflows in Unreal Engine.

  • Experience designing systemic puzzles, physics-based interactions, or environmental features that support multiple solutions and emergent multiplayer play.

  • Experience profiling and optimizing gameplay scripts and level content.

The Team:

  • This role reports to the Design Manager.

How We Work

We believe great games are built by people who care deeply about both the work and one another. Our values guide how we collaborate, solve problems, make decisions, and grow together. They're practical behaviors, not slogans, and they're part of how we hire, give feedback, and support one another every day.

We're looking for teammates who are excited to:

  • Stay curious and ask thoughtful questions.

  • Adapt when plans change.

  • Exercise good judgment rather than chase perfection.

  • Care for the success of the whole team, not just their own work.

  • Pursue ambitious goals while remaining humble enough to keep learning.

  • Commit fully to the shared adventure we're building together.

You'll Thrive Here If...

  • You enjoy asking questions before jumping to conclusions.

  • You adapt comfortably when priorities evolve.

  • You balance ambition with pragmatism.

  • You communicate thoughtfully and seek feedback.

  • You care about helping your teammates succeed.

  • You embrace uncertainty as part of creating something new.

Please Note: Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States or Canada. Gardens cannot assist with work authorizations or work visas. Applicants must also be willing to work within North American time zones (EST–PST).

Our Interview Process

(all interviews are 1 hour video calls on Google Meet unless otherwise noted)

  • Step 1: People Operations Introduction

  • Step 2: Hiring Manager Interview

  • Step 3: Panel Interview (3 - 1 Hour Sections)

  • Step 4: Gardeners Debrief

  • Step 5: Offer

Life at Gardens

Gardens is a fully distributed game studio founded by creators behind titles including Journey, What Remains of Edith Finch, Blaseball, Dustforce, Ashen, Guild Wars 2, Baldur’s Gate 3, and more.

We're developing our flagship project: a multiplayer fantasy adventure inspired by the friendships, discoveries, and unforgettable stories that emerge when people explore together.

We believe the best ideas come from teams with diverse experiences, perspectives, backgrounds, and ways of thinking. Every Gardener helps shape not only what we build, but how we build it.

Each of us arrives by a different path, bringing unique experiences, perspectives, and ways of seeing the world. That range is part of what makes our games and our studio better than any one of us could build alone.

Gardens Offers:

  • Competitive salaries and pay transparency

  • Stock options

  • Medical, dental, and vision coverage (100% for individuals, 90% for dependents)

  • Life insurance, short-term and long-term disability, and additional benefits

  • 401(k) contributions (U.S.) / RRSP + DPSP contributions (Canada)

  • Paid parental leave

  • A fully distributed remote studio across North American time zones

Benefits and perks listed may vary depending on the nature of your employment with Gardens and the country in which you work.

Physical Requirements: This is a primarily sedentary, remote role requiring the ability to remain stationary and perform computer-based work for extended periods, including sustained use of monitors, keyboards, mice, and game controllers for a minimum of six hours per day. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the role. Gardens is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities.

Encouragement: We believe that diverse perspectives make our team stronger and our games better. If you're excited about this role but don't meet every single qualification, we encourage you to apply anyway.

Research consistently shows that talented people, particularly women, people of color, and those from historically underrepresented communities are less likely to apply unless they meet every listed requirement. We care far more about curiosity, growth, and a willingness to learn than checking every box.

jobs.description:
Job Title: Senior Director, Patient Reported Outcomes

Job Location: Remote (US)

Job Location Type: Remote

Job Contract Type: Full-time

Job Seniority Level:

BeOne continues to grow at a rapid pace with challenging and exciting opportunities for experienced professionals. When considering candidates, we look for scientific and business professionals who are highly motivated, collaborative, and most importantly, share our passionate interest in fighting cancer.

General Description:


The Senior Director, Patient Reported Outcomes (PRO), is a senior scientific and strategic leader accountable for developing and executing integrated evidence-generation strategies that demonstrate the humanistic value of BeOne Medicines therapies. The role provides enterprise-level PRO leadership across one or more assets, indications, therapeutic areas, or regions and ensures that high-priority evidence needs are represented in integrated evidence plans, medical strategies, clinical development plans, and value and access strategies. The Senior Director influences portfolio and asset decisions, leads complex global humanistic programs, governs scientific quality and investment, and builds organizational capability through people leadership, matrix leadership, and external scientific engagement.


Working across Clinical Development, Medical Affairs, Global Value, Access and Pricing, Biostatistics, Data Science, Patient-Reported Outcomes, Regulatory, Safety, Publications, Legal, Compliance, Privacy, and regional teams, the incumbent translates evidence gaps into prioritized, feasible research programs. The role is accountable for strategic alignment, scientific rigor, compliant execution, timely delivery, budget stewardship, and effective communication of PRO evidence to internal decision-makers and appropriate external stakeholders.



Essential Functions of the Job:


Strategy and Portfolio Leadership

  • Own and provide senior leadership for global or regional PRO strategy across assigned assets, programs, therapeutic areas, or portfolios throughout the product lifecycle.
  • Shape integrated evidence plans by identifying, prioritizing, and revisiting evidence gaps in collaboration with cross-functional leadership and evidence-generating functions.
  • Ensure PRO perspectives are incorporated into asset strategy, clinical development plans, medical plans, lifecycle planning, launch preparation, reimbursement strategy, and annual operating and budget processes.
  • Advise senior leaders and governance bodies on PRO evidence priorities, investment trade-offs, methodological options, feasibility, timing, and risk.
  • Anticipate changes in healthcare systems, payer and health technology assessment expectations, data availability, methodological standards, and the competitive landscape, and translate those changes into strategic recommendations.

Scientific and Methodological Leadership

  • Provide executive scientific oversight for PRO real-world evidence, observational research, comparative effectiveness and safety research, burden-of-illness studies, patient preference research, health economic models, indirect treatment comparisons, evidence syntheses, and value communication deliverables.
  • Guide the selection and implementation of fit-for-purpose patient-reported outcome and other clinical outcome assessment strategies in partnership with PRO and Clinical Development experts.
  • Ensure research questions, protocols, analysis plans, models, and interpretations are scientifically rigorous, reproducible, transparent, and aligned with intended decision needs.
  • Provide senior review and approval, within delegated authority, of concepts, protocols, statistical analysis plans, technical reports, models, publications, and executive presentations.
  • Sponsor innovation in PRO, analytical, and data-science methods while ensuring appropriate validation, governance, and business relevance.

Program Governance and Execution

  • Lead a portfolio of complex, high-impact evidence-generation programs from concept through results dissemination and project closure.
  • Set priorities, decision rights, milestones, quality expectations, and escalation pathways for internal teams and external research partners.
  • Oversee project budgets, forecasts, contracts, vendor performance, timelines, risks, and resource allocation, and take timely corrective action when objectives are at risk.
  • Ensure appropriate cross-functional review and compliance with applicable legal, ethical, privacy, safety, regulatory, publication, data-governance, and company requirements.
  • Establish fit-for-purpose quality controls and independent technical review for complex analyses, models, and high-impact deliverables.
  • Ensure balanced interpretation of findings, including uncertainty, missingness, bias, confounding, generalizability, sensitivity analyses, and study limitations.

Cross-Functional and Executive Influence

  • Serve as the senior PRO partner to asset teams, medical and development leadership, access teams, governance committees, and regional stakeholders.
  • Build alignment across functions and geographies when priorities, evidence needs, timelines, or methodological perspectives differ.
  • Translate complex scientific and economic evidence into clear implications and recommendations for executive, clinical, payer, regulatory, and nontechnical audiences.
  • Facilitate timely decisions by framing options, trade-offs, dependencies, risks, and recommended actions.
  • Contribute to business development, due diligence, portfolio assessment, and external partnership evaluations, as assigned.
  • Lead or oversee publication and scientific communication strategies for assigned PRO programs in partnership with Publications and cross-functional stakeholders.
  • Represent BeOne Medicines at scientific congresses, professional associations, advisory forums, and other appropriate external engagements.
  • Build credible relationships with researchers, clinicians, payers, health economists, patient organizations, and other external experts in accordance with company policies.
  • Advance the company’s scientific reputation through high-quality research, peer-reviewed publications, presentations, and responsible methodological leadership.

People and Organizational Leadership

  • Lead, coach, and develop direct reports and provide matrix leadership to cross-functional colleagues, contractors, and external research teams.
  • Set clear objectives, provide actionable feedback, support development planning, and create an inclusive environment that promotes accountability, collaboration, and scientific challenge.
  • Assess capability and capacity needs and recommend hiring, external support, training, tools, standards, and operating-model improvements.
  • Promote consistent PRO practices, knowledge sharing, reusable resources, and continuous improvement across global and regional teams.
  • Demonstrate sound judgment, integrity, financial stewardship, and accountability for decisions and commitments.

Supervisory Responsibilities

  • Manages and develops one or more employees, as assigned, and provides senior functional direction to matrix teams, contractors, and external research partners.
  • Accountable for goal setting, performance and development discussions, workload prioritization, succession and capability planning, and a respectful, inclusive team environment.

Education Required:

  • Advanced degree in health economics, outcomes research, epidemiology, biostatistics, public health, psychometrics, pharmacy, medicine, or a related quantitative or clinical discipline, or equivalent education and relevant experience.

Required Qualifications:

  • Advanced Degree (Masters, PhD, PharmD, PhD, MD) with 10 or more years of progressively responsible experience in PRO, RWE, outcomes research, epidemiology, market access evidence, medical affairs, clinical research, or a related field, including substantial biopharmaceutical or healthcare-sector experience.
  • Demonstrated success defining and executing evidence strategies for complex assets, therapeutic areas, or portfolios in a global or multi-regional environment.
  • Deep expertise in several relevant methods, including observational study design, causal inference, comparative effectiveness, economic modeling, indirect treatment comparisons, evidence synthesis, PRO/COA methods, patient preference research, or analysis of claims, electronic health records, registries, or clinical-trial data.
  • Proven ability to influence senior leaders, governance bodies, and cross-functional teams without relying solely on formal authority.
  • Demonstrated leadership of complex programs, budgets, vendors, risks, competing priorities, people, and matrix teams.
  • Strong scientific communication record and excellent written, verbal, presentation, negotiation, and stakeholder-management skills.
  • Working knowledge of applicable research, privacy, safety, publication, compliance, and data-governance expectations.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Doctoral degree in a relevant discipline.
  • Significant oncology and hematology experience.
  • Experience with health technology assessment, reimbursement, regulatory, or value communication strategies across major global markets.
  • Demonstrated publication record and external scientific presence in PRO, epidemiology, health economics, or related methods.
  • Experience establishing functional standards, governance, centers of excellence, or enterprise-wide evidence-generation capabilities.
  • Experience with statistical or analytical software and critical review of code outputs, models, data specifications, tables, and figures.

Computer Skills:

  • PC, including MS Office Suite and MS Teams.
  • Proficiency with productivity, collaboration, presentation, project-management, and document-management platforms.
  • Familiarity with analytical tools, real-world data sources, economic-modeling applications, literature-review platforms, or regulated content systems is preferred.

Travel:

  • Approximately 25–30%, including domestic and international travel as business needs require.
  • Ability to participate in meetings across time zones and respond flexibly to critical business needs.
  • Ability to perform the essential functions of the role with or without reasonable accommodation.

Additional Position Information:

  • Reports to the Vice President, Integrative Evidence Generation and Health Economics, Global Medical Affairs.
  • Work location: Remote.
  • People-manager role with direct reports and/or matrix leadership, as assigned.

Global Competencies

When we exhibit our values of Patients First, Driving Excellence, Bold Ingenuity and Collaborative Spirit, through our twelve global competencies below, we help get more affordable medicines to more patients around the world.

  • Fosters Teamwork
  • Provides and Solicits Honest and Actionable Feedback
  • Self-Awareness
  • Acts Inclusively
  • Demonstrates Initiative
  • Entrepreneurial Mindset
  • Continuous Learning
  • Embraces Change
  • Results-Oriented
  • Analytical Thinking/Data Analysis
  • Financial Excellence
  • Communicates with Clarity
Salary Range: $222,000.00 - $292,000.00 annually

BeOne is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices. Actual compensation packages are determined by several factors that are unique to each candidate, including but not limited to job-related skills, depth of experience, certifications, relevant education or training, and specific work location. Packages may vary by location due to differences in the cost of labor. The recruiter can share more about the specific salary range for a preferred location during the hiring process. Please note that the listed range reflects the base salary or hourly range only. Non-Commercial roles are eligible to participate in the annual bonus plan, and Commercial roles are eligible to participate in an incentive compensation plan. All Company employees have the opportunity to own shares of BeOne Medicines Ltd. stock because all employees are eligible for discretionary equity awards and to voluntarily participate in the Employee Stock Purchase Plan. The Company has a comprehensive benefits package that includes Medical, Dental, Vision, 401(k), FSA/HSA, Life Insurance, Paid Time Off, and Wellness.

The original mission of BJAK is we believe people deserve smarter ways to plan, save and grow their money. This is the origin of our name.

• Provide strategic support and special project leadership on behalf of the SVP of Utilization Management and Chief Medical Officer.
